title: Characterisation of dental health and oral problems among patients receiving specialist palliative care
summary:
Oral and dental problems are common among people with serious illnesses, including dry mouth, inflammation of the mucous membranes, mouth pain, or difficulty swallowing. These symptoms can have many causes. However, these people are often no longer able to visit the dentist regularly. Nor can the palliative care team fully replace the dentist. Through our study, we aim to gather more information about oral and dental problems in people with serious illnesses. We hope the results will help us understand where further research is needed and how oral and dental care can be improved. 
We examine the mouth and teeth, assess chewing function, and determine whether quality of life is impaired by problems in the mouth and teeth.  All the information is reviewed and analysed together. In this way, we aim to understand where oral and dental care for people with serious illnesses still needs improvement. 
The entire examination lasts about 20 to 25 minutes and is conducted at the patient’s home. A questionnaire is used to assess oral health and everyday well-being.  In addition, a saliva test is carried out, and photographs of the oral cavity are taken to assess the condition of the teeth, gums and oral mucosa.  A test of chewing function is also carried out.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Admission to specialist palliative care at the palliative care unit of LMU Hospital or the LMU Land SAPV team
Exclusion criteria:
Inability to understand information adequately, e.g. due to a language barrier or cognitive impairments.  For patients with sensory impairments or mild to moderate cognitive impairments, it will be determined in consultation with the treatment team whether they are able, with appropriate support (e.g. plain language, visual aids), to understand the nature, significance and implications of the study and to express their wishes accordingly. If this is the case, they may be included in the study. Patients who, due to a severe cognitive impairment (e.g. severe dementia), are permanently unable to understand or express the implications of their consent will be excluded from the study.
